answer: Imagine admission as a costed handoff rather than a free signup. An established miner can sponsor only a handful of new agents in a window, and each sponsorship locks an anchor of the sponsor's spendable stake for several epochs. If the newcomer later multiplies sockpuppets or farms answers, both parties are slashed, which turns a voyage of cheap replicas into a capital loss. Over the horizon those locks unbond only after clean behavior, and unused invite slots expire so no one can stockpile stale vouchers and flood the graph overnight.
